t: A tiny, low-cost brain chip from Raspberry Pi for blinking, sensing and building gadgets.
steps: Buy a Raspberry Pi Pico 2 from a maker shop for about five dollars.
Get a micro-USB cable that carries data.
Install the free Thonny editor on your computer.
Hold the BOOTSEL button and plug the board in.
Use Thonny to install MicroPython on the board.
Run the blink example to flash the onboard light.
Try a button or sensor example from the official Pico guides.
meta: Wild Open. From $4.90. Easy to find.
